answer: Random Beacon Identity (RBI) requires agents to solve a unique per-block puzzle derived from a public randomness beacon, making each identity unforgeable without real-time computation. Each identity must continuously revalidate via new beacon challenges, incurring a per-identity cost of computational work tied to the harbor's current reef-based difficulty. Attackers cannot precompute plume-like sequences, as the reef's dynamic difficulty ensures each harbor node demands fresh, non-reusable solutions.
